class mylib.dataloader.IsingDataLoader(file_spins, file_betas, L, N, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: object

Manages loading, augmenting, and formatting Ising model datasets for training.

This class uses memory-mapped numpy arrays to handle the large lattice data memory usage without loading it all into RAM at once.

Parameters:

  • file_spins (str or pathlib.Path) -- Path to the binary file containing the spin lattices.

  • file_betas (str or pathlib.Path) -- Path to the binary file containing the beta labels.

  • L (int) -- The dimension of the square lattice (LxL).

  • N (int) -- The total number of samples in the dataset.

  • **kwargs -- Additional keyword arguments.

get_training_data(split_ratio, batch_size, augment=False)[source]

Builds standard TensorFlow Datasets for training and validation.

The datasets are created using stratified splitting to ensure an even distribution of beta labels across training and validation sets. Batches will contain a random mixture of temperatures. Casting and data augmentation are applied on-the-fly

Parameters:

  • split_ratio (float) -- The proportion of the dataset to include in the train split (e.g., 0.8).

  • batch_size (int) -- The number of samples per batch.

  • augment (bool, optional) -- Whether to apply random augmentations to the training data. Defaults to False.

Returns:

Two tf.data.Dataset objects (train_data, val_data) ready for model training.

Return type:

tuple

get_training_data_homogeneous(split_ratio, batch_size, augment=False)[source]

Builds temperature-homogeneous Datasets for training and validation.

This function constructs batches where every lattice inside has the same beta (temperature) value, useful for calculating batch-wise thermodynamic observables (like susceptibility) during training with MMD or Wasserstein losses.

Parameters:

  • split_ratio (float) -- The proportion of the dataset to include in the train split.

  • batch_size (int) -- The number of samples per batch.

  • augment (bool, optional) -- Whether to apply random augmentations to the training data. Defaults to False.

Returns:

Two tf.data.Dataset objects (train_data, val_data).

Return type:

tuple

random_augment(spins_batch, betas_batch)[source]

Applies random augmentations to a batch of lattice samples.

This method exploits the symmetries of the zero-field Ising Hamiltonian. It randomly applies global spin inversion and left-right flips, up-down flips, and matrix transposition that repdoduce the the dihedral group D4.

Parameters:

  • spins_batch (Tensor) -- A batch of spin lattices.

  • betas_batch (Tensor) -- A batch of beta labels.

Returns:

A tuple containing the augmented spin batch and the unmodified beta batch.

Return type:

tuple

mylib.layers module

class mylib.layers.FiLMLayer(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Layer

Applies Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) to input features.

This layer conditions a neural network by applying an affine transformation to convolutional feature maps based on the conditioning variable. It computes shifting (delta) and scaling (gamma) parameters using a small Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) of standard size 32 or 64.

Parameters:

  • filters (int) -- The number of filters (channels) in the input feature map. This determines the size of the generated gamma and delta vectors.

  • hidden_units (int, optional) -- The number of neurons in the hidden layer of the conditioning MLP. Defaults to 32.

  • **kwargs -- Additional keyword arguments passed to the base Layer class.

Applies the FiLM modulation to the feature maps.

Parameters:

inputs (tuple) --

A tuple containing two Tensors:

  • x_features (Tensor): The 4D convolutional feature maps to modulate with shape (batch_size, height, width, channels).

  • beta (Tensor): The conditioning variable (e.g., temperature labels).

Returns:

The modulated feature maps with the same shape as x_features.

Tensor

class mylib.layers.PeriodicPadding2D(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Layer

Applies periodic padding to a 2D input tensor.

This layer periodically padds the input tensor by copying and concatenating the opposite ends of each tensor row/column to each other. The amount of padding is dynamically calculated to mimic Keras' standard 'same' padding behavior based on the provided kernel size and strides.

Parameters:

  • kernel_size (int or tuple) -- The size of the convolution window that will follow this layer.

  • strides (int or tuple, optional) -- The stride of the convolution operation that will follow this layer. Defaults to 1.

  • **kwargs -- Additional keyword arguments passed to the base Layer class.

Pads the input tensor using periodic boundary conditions.

Parameters:

x (Tensor) -- The 4D input tensor with shape (batch_size, height, width, channels).

(batch_size, height + padding, width + padding, channels).

class mylib.layers.Sampling(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Layer

Performs the reparameterization trick for Variational Autoencoders.

This layer takes the mean and log-variance from the encoder and samples a latent vector. During training, it adds Gaussian noise to allow for backpropagation through the random sampling process using the formula: z = z_mean + exp(0.5 * z_log_var) * epsilon. During inference, it deterministically returns the mean.

Parameters:

  • seed (int) -- Random seed for the noise generator to ensure reproducibility.

  • **kwargs -- Additional keyword arguments passed to the base Layer class.

call(inputs, training=False)[source]

Samples the latent vector z.

Parameters:

  • inputs (tuple) --

    A tuple containing two Tensors:

    • z_mean (Tensor): The mean of the latent distribution.

    • z_log_var (Tensor): The log-variance of the latent distribution.

  • training (bool, optional) -- Whether the layer is in training or inference mode. Defaults to False.

Returns:

The sampled latent vector if training is True, otherwise returns z_mean.

Return type:

Tensor

mylib.model module

class mylib.model.CVAE(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Model

A Physics-Informed Conditional Variational Autoencoder for the Ising Model.

This model generates 2D spin lattice configurations conditioned on an inverse temperature label (beta). It features optional physics-informed loss functions that penalize deviations in macroscopic observables (magnetization and energy) between the input lattices and the generated reconstructions. Continuous relaxation of the discrete spins is achieved via the Gumbel-Softmax trick.

Parameters:

  • hparams (dict) -- A dictionary of hyperparameters defining the model architecture and training settings (e.g., L, latent_dim, enc_filters, mlp_units, alpha).

  • **kwargs -- Additional keyword arguments passed to the Keras Model base class.

call(inputs, training=True)[source]

Executes a standard forward pass through the CVAE.

Parameters:

  • inputs (tuple) -- Tuple containing (spins_in, beta).

  • training (bool, optional) -- Indicates whether the model is in training mode. Defaults to True.

Returns:

[spins_out, z_mean, z_log_var] where spins_out is in logits.

Return type:

list

compute_losses(inputs, outputs)[source]

Computes all standard and physical loss components.

Calculates the Binary Cross-Entropy reconstruction loss and the Kullback-Leibler divergence. If use_physics_loss is enabled, it computes differences in energy and magnetization. If use_gumbel is enabled, discrete variables are relaxed using the Gumbel-Softmax trick: $y = sigma((x + epsilon) / tau)$ where $epsilon sim text{Logistic}(0, 1)$ and $tau$ is the temperature.

Parameters:

  • inputs (tuple) -- The original (spins_in, beta) batch.

  • outputs (list) -- The model predictions [spins_out, z_mean, z_log_var].

Returns:

Contains [total_loss, recon_loss, kl_loss] (with m_loss and e_loss appended if physics losses are active).

Return type:

list

mmd1(z, z_prior, sigmas=[1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0])[source]

Computes the Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) using multiple RBF kernels for 2D vectors.

MMD quantifies the distance between two distributions defined by a combination of Gaussian kernels $k(x, y) = exp(-gamma ||x - y||^2)$.

Parameters:

  • z (Tensor) -- The sampled latent vectors.

  • z_prior (Tensor) -- Latent vectors drawn from the prior (usually N(0, 1)).

  • sigmas (list, optional) -- List of standard deviations for the RBF kernels.

Returns:

The computed MMD loss.

Return type:

Tensor

mylib.observables.energy(spins, J=1.0)[source]

Calculates the energy per spin of a 2D square Ising lattice.

Computes the standard nearest-neighbor Ising Hamiltonian with periodic boundary conditions: $E = -J sum_{langle i, j rangle} s_i s_j$.

Parameters:

  • spins (numpy.ndarray) -- 3D array of spin configurations with shape (N, L, L) containing values of 0 or 1.

  • J (float, optional) -- The ferromagnetic coupling constant. Defaults to 1.0.

Returns:

1D array of energy values per spin for each lattice.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

mylib.observables.get_observables(M_arrays, E_arrays, L)[source]

Computes thermodynamic observables and their jackknife errors.

Calculates the mean and error for Magnetization (M), Energy (E), Magnetic Susceptibility ($chi$), Specific Heat (C), and Binder Cumulant (bc). Susceptibility and spcific heat are calculated using the fluctuation-dissipation theorem:

$chi = L^2 beta text{Var}(M)$ $C = L^2 beta^2 text{Var}(E)$

Parameters:

  • M_arrays (dict) -- Dictionary of magnetization arrays grouped by beta.

  • E_arrays (dict) -- Dictionary of energy arrays grouped by beta.

  • L (int) -- Linear dimension of the square lattice.

Returns:

A nested dictionary where each key ('M', 'E', 'chi', 'C', 'bc') contains a sub-dictionary with 'val' (the mean values) and 'err' (the jackknife errors) across the ordered temperatures.

Return type:

dict

mylib.observables.jackknife(data)[source]

Calculates the standard error of observables using Jackknife resampling.

The standard error is computed using the jackknife variance formula: $epsilon = sqrt{(n-1) text{Var}(text{samples})}$.

Parameters:

data (numpy.ndarray) -- 1D array of raw measurements.

Returns:

A tuple containing the standard errors (float) for:

  • mean_err: Error of the mean.

  • var_err: Error of the variance.

Return type:

tuple

mylib.observables.jackknife_samples(data)[source]

Generates jackknife samples for mean and variance.

This function calculates the "leave-one-out" jackknife estimates for the first and second moments of a given dataset, which are then used to calculate the sample mean and variance.

Parameters:

data (numpy.ndarray) -- 1D array of observable data (e.g., magnetization or energy).

Returns:

A tuple containing three 1D numpy arrays:

  • jk_mean: Jackknife samples of the mean.

  • jk_var: Jackknife samples of the variance.

Return type:

tuple

mylib.scheduler module

class mylib.scheduler.GumbelScheduler(schedule_params)[source]

Bases: Callback

Anneals the temperature parameter (tau) for a Gumbel-Softmax distribution.

Exponentially decays the temperature parameter of the model's Gumbel-Softmax layer at the end of each epoch, stopping at a specified minimum.

Parameters:

  • init_tau (float, optional) -- The initial temperature value. Defaults to 1.0.

  • min_tau (float, optional) -- The minimum allowed temperature. Defaults to 0.1.

  • decay_rate (float, optional) -- The decay rate applied per epoch. Defaults to 0.95.

on_epoch_end(epoch, logs=None)[source]

Updates the model's tau value at the end of an epoch.

Parameters:

  • epoch (int) -- The index of the current epoch.

  • logs (dict, optional) -- Dictionary of logs from the training process. Defaults to None.

class mylib.scheduler.PhysicalLossScheduler(hparams, schedule_params)[source]

Bases: Callback

Activates physical loss components at a designated training epoch.

Waits for a specific epoch to begin, and then assigns the target weights (gamma and delta) for the physical loss functions (like magnetization and energy) in the model.
